Find the track that best fits your idea, then submit your project by Tuesday , July 21 at 5:00 PM PT . Whether it's an app, agent, website, game, workflow, or something entirely new, your project should fit into one of the following tracks: Apps for your life Consumer apps for everyday life — from productivity and creativity to home, family, travel, health, and personal finance. Developer tools Tools for developers, including testing, DevOps, agentic workflows, and security. A PURCHASE OR PAYMENT WILL NOT INCREASE YOUR CHANCES OF WINNING. SUBMISSION OF ANY ENTRY CONSTITUTES AGREEMENT TO THESE OFFICIAL RULES AS A CONTRACT BETWEEN ENTRANT (AND EACH INDIVIDUAL MEMBER OF ENTRANT), THE HACKATHON SPONSOR, AND DEVPOST. 1. Dates and Timing Registration Period: July 9th, 2026 (10:00 am Pacific Time) – July 21st, 2026 (5:00 pm Pacific Time) (“Registration Period”). Submission Period: July 13th, 2026 (9:00 am Pacific Time) – July 21st, 2026 (5:00 pm Pacific Time) (“Submission Period”). Judging Period: July 22nd, 2026 (10:00 am Pacific Time) – August 5th, 2026 (5:00 pm Pacific Time) (“Judging Period”). Winners Announced: On or around August 12th, 2026 (2:00 pm Pacific Time). 2. Sponsor and Administrator Sponsor: OpenAI OpCo, LLC, 1455 3rd Street, San Francisco, CA 94158 Administrator: Devpost, Inc. (“Devpost”), 250 Broadway, Floor 24, New York, NY 10007 3. Eligibility The Hackathon IS open to: Individuals who are at least the age of majority where they reside as of the time of entry (“Eligible Individuals”); Individuals who are residents of countries and territories that currently support access to OpenAI’s API services listed here and are not excluded below: Supported countries and territories | OpenAI API Parents or Guardians of students under the age of 18 (or under the age of majority in their jurisdiction of residence at the time of entry); Teams of Eligible Individuals (“Teams”); and Organizations based in countries and territories that currently support access to OpenAI’s API services listed here: https://platform.openai.com/docs/supported-countries. (including corporations, not-for-profit corporations and other nonprofit organizations, limited liability companies, partnerships, and other legal entities) that exist and have been organized or incorporated at the time of entry. (the above are collectively, “Entrants”) An Eligible Individual may join more than one Team or Organization and an Eligible Individual who is part of a Team or Organization may also enter the Hackathon on an individual basis. If a Team or Organization is entering the Hackathon, they must appoint and authorize one individual (the “Representative”) to represent, act, and enter a Submission, on their behalf. By entering a Submission on behalf of a Team or Organization you represent and warrant that you are the Representative authorized to act on behalf of your Team or Organization. The Hackathon IS NOT open to: Individuals or organizations who are not residents of, or Organizations domiciled in, a country, state, province or territory listed here: https://platform.openai.com/docs/supported-countries Individuals who are residents of, or Organizations domiciled in, a country, state, province or territory where the laws of the United States or local law prohibits participating or receiving a prize in the Hackathon (including, but not limited to, Brazil, Quebec, Russia, Crimea, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria and any other country designated by the United States Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control) Organizations involved with the design, production, paid promotion, execution, or distribution of the Hackathon, including the Sponsor and Administrator (“Promotion Entities”). Employees, representatives and agents** of such Promotion Entities, and all members of their immediate family or household* Any other individual involved with the design, production, promotion, execution, or distribution of the Hackathon, and each member of their immediate family or household* Any Judge (defined below), or company or individual that employs a Judge Any parent company, subsidiary, or other affiliate*** of any organization described above Any other individual or organization whose participation in the Hackathon would create, in the sole discretion of the Sponsor and/or Administrator, a real or apparent conflict of interest *The members of an individual’s immediate family include the individual’s spouse, children and stepchildren, parents and stepparents, and siblings and stepsiblings. The members of an individual’s household include any other person that shares the same residence as the individual for at least three (3) months out of the year. **Agents include individuals or organizations that in creating a Submission to the Hackathon, are acting on behalf of, and at the direction of, a Promotion Entity through a contractual or similar relationship. ***An affiliate is: (a) an organization that is under common control, sharing a common majority or controlling owner, or common management; or (b) an organization that has a substantial ownership in, or is substantially owned by the other organization. 4. How To Enter Entrants may enter by visiting openai.devpost.com (“Hackathon Website”) and following the below steps: Register for the Hackathon on the Hackathon Website by clicking the “Join Hackathon” button. To complete registration, sign up to create a free Devpost account, or log in with an existing Devpost account. This will enable you to receive important updates and to create your Submission. Entrants will obtain access to the required developer tools/platform and complete a Project described below in Project Requirements. Use of the developer tools will be subject to the license agreement related thereto. Entry in the Hackathon constitutes consent for the Sponsor and Devpost to collect and maintain an entrant’s personal information for the purpose of operating and publicizing the Hackathon. Obtain access to the required developer tools by completing the following: If your free ts are exhausted, Entrants may request $100 in free credits to build their Project for the Hackathon while supplies last and subject to approval. Free credits can only be requested by Entrants registered for the Hackathon. To request credits, complete the form at: https://forms.gle/Ncu6iGkaHq1SwUmEA by July 17th at 12pm PT . Codex credits and credits are not redeemable for cash and must be used by July 21st at 5pm PT . Optionally, install the Devpost Plugin from the Hackathon Website. Use of the Devpost Plugin is not required to enter or win. See Section 5 (Devpost Plugin) for terms of use. Sign up for an OpenAI account and download Codex. All credits and credits, and all use of OpenAI's services, are subject to OpenAI's Terms of Use ( openai.com/policies/row-terms-of-use ), OpenAI's Business Terms governing API and developer use, OpenAI's Service Credit Terms governing credits redeemable for OpenAI services, and OpenAI's Usage Policies ( openai.com/policies/usage-policies ). NOTE: Any additional charges incurred by the Entrant for the use of OpenAI products or services beyond the provided credits or credits are the responsibility of the Entrant. Entrants are encouraged to monitor their usage so as not to incur additional charges. Complete and enter all of the required fields on the “Enter a Submission” page of the Hackathon Website (each a “Submission”) during the Submission Period and follow the requirements below. Project Requirements What to Create: Build any project with Codex and GPT 5.6 that fits into one of the following tracks. Some examples include web and native applications, backend tools, agent plugins (skills, mcps, tools) or games. Apps for Your Life. Consumer apps for everyday life — from productivity and creativity to home, family, travel, health, and personal finance. Work and Productivity. Tools that make teams faster or more effective, from workflow automation and customer support to analytics, sales, and back-office operations. Developer Tools. Tools for developers, including testing, DevOps, agentic workflows, and security. Education. Projects that specifically push forward AI for education - either helping students, teachers, or educational organizations . Functionality: The Project must be capable of being successfully installed and running consistently on the platform for which it is intended and must function as depicted in the video and/or expressed in the text description. Platforms: A submitted Project must run on the platform for which it is intended and which is specified in the Submission Requirements. New & Existing: Projects must be either newly created during the Hackathon Submission Period or, if the Project existed prior to the Submission Period, must have been meaningfully extended using Codex and/or GPT-5.6 after the Submission Period start date. Pre-existing Projects will be evaluated only on work added during the Submission Period. Entrants with pre-existing Projects must provide clear documentation distinguishing prior work from new work, including evidence that Codex and/or GPT-5.6 was used within the Submission Period (e.g., timestamped Codex session logs, dated commit history, or equivalent). Third Party Integrations: If a Project integrates any third-party SDK, APIs and/or data, Entrant must be authorized to use them in accordance with any terms and conditions or licensing requirements of the tool. Submission Requirements Submissions to the Hackathon must meet the following requirements: Include a Project built with the required developer tools and meets the above Project Requirements. Choose the category that best aligns with your project Include a text description that should explain the features and functionality of your Project. Include a demonstration video of your Project. The video portion of the Submission: should be less than three (3) minutes. Judges are not required to watch beyond three minutes must include a clear demo with audio that covers what you built and how you used Codex and GPT-5.6 must be uploaded to and made publicly visible on YouTube, and a link to the video must be provided on the submission form on the Hackathon Website; and must not include third party trademarks, or copyrighted music or other material unless the Entrant has permission to use such material. Provide a URL to your code repository for judging and testing. The repository must be either public (with relevant licensing) or private and shared with testing@devpost.com and build-week-event@openai.

excerpt: OpenAI Build Week: Join a global week of building with Codex - Devpost Log in Sign up Join a hackathon Devpost Participate in our public hackathons Hackathons Projects Devpost for Teams Access your company's private hackathons Login Host a hackathon Devpost Grow your developer ecosystem and promote your platform Host a public hackathon Devpost for Teams Drive innovation, collaboration, and retention within your organization Host an internal hackathon By use case AI hackathons Customer hackathons Employee hackathons Public hackathons Resources Blog Insights into hackathon planning and participation Customer stories Inspiration from peers and other industry leaders Planning guides Best practices for planning online and in-person hackathons Webinars & events Upcoming events and on-demand recordings Help desk Common questions and support documentation Join a hackathon Devpost Participate in our public hackathons Hackathons Projects Devpost for Teams Access your company's private hackathons Login Host a hackathon Devpost Grow your developer ecosystem and promote your platform Host a public hackathon Devpost for Teams Drive innovation, collaboration, and retention within your organization Host an internal hackathon By use case AI hackathons Customer hackathons Employee hackathons Public hackathons Resources Blog Insights into hackathon planning and participation Customer stories Inspiration from peers and other industry leaders Planning guides Best practices for planning online and in-person hackathons Webinars & events Upcoming events and on-demand recordings Help desk Common questions and support documentation Log in Sign up OpenAI Build Week Deadline: Jul 21, 2026 @ 5:00pm PDT Join hackathon Descend Overview My projects Participants (42062) Resources Rules Project gallery Updates Discussions FAQs General Can I participate solo or on a team? Yes. You can enter as an individual, a team, or an organization. How many members are allowed per team? There is no limit on team size but note some prizes have their own team-size restrictions, so check individual prize details. Can I work on a project I already started? Yes. If your project existed before the hackathon, you'll need to clearly document what's new, including evidence that Codex and/or GPT-5.6 was used during the Submission Period (timestamped session logs, commit history, etc.). What categories can I enter? There are four categories: Apps for Your Life Work and Productivity Developer Tools Education Pick the track that fits your project best. If your project could fit more than one, choose the closest match — each project can only be entered into one track. Do judges test my project? They may, but they're not required to. If they do, they'll use the demo link, sandbox, or test account you provide. Make sure your README and instructions are clear. Can I update my submission after the deadline? No changes can be made to your submission after the Submission Period ends on July 21 at 5:00 PM PT. I've never used Codex before. Can I still compete? Absolutely. Sign up for an OpenAI account, download Codex, request your free Codex credits, and dive in. The plugin has resources and commands to help you get oriented. Build Week is as much about exploring as it is competing. Do I need a paid plan to participate? No. You can participate with a Free plan. Free users have access to GPT‑5.6 Terra in Codex, and any Codex credits provided for the competition can be applied to extend usage for models available to your plan. Do I need to use 5.6 for my whole project? No. You can use any model you want for your project as long as you've used 5.6 for a part of it Do I need to be a professional developer to enter? No. The Education track in particular welcomes projects from students, educators, and learners. All tracks are open to anyone who meets the eligibility requirements. Can my team be in different countries? Yes, as long as each team member meets the individual eligibility requirements for their country of residence. Can I use open source libraries or existing frameworks? Yes. Standard development tools, libraries, and frameworks are allowed. You must comply with any applicable open source licenses, and you need to disclose any pre-existing code or third-party work in your submission. What if I want to build a plugin or developer tool as my project? That's a great fit for the Developer Tools track. Just make sure to include installation instructions, supported platforms, and a testing path for judges who won't rebuild it from scratch. Tools Do I have to use Codex? Yes. Codex usage is required and must be demonstrated in your submission including your text description, demo video and highlight where Codex accelerated your workflow, where you made key product, engineering, or design decisions in your README. You'll need to provide a /feedback Codex Session ID from the primary thread where you built your project, and specifically, your demo video must include audio explaining how you used Codex. Do I have to use GPT-5.6? Yes. Your project must use GPT-5.6. Judges will look for evidence of this in your demo video and code repository; make sure it's clearly referenced in your README. Can I use other models or tools alongside GPT-5.6 and Codex? You can use standard libraries, frameworks, and third-party SDKs as long as you're authorized to use them. But your project must meaningfully use both Codex and GPT-5.6 — they can't be incidental or decorative. What counts as "using Codex"? Building your project with Codex — whether through the ChatGPT app, the Codex CLI, the IDE extension, or the SDK. You'll verify this by submitting the /feedback Session ID from the main thread where you did the majority of your core development. How do I get the /feedback Session ID? In Codex, run /feedback in the thread where you did the majority of your core work. This will generate a Session ID (a unique identifier for that thread). Copy it and paste it into the submission form. You should use the thread where most of your core functionality was built — not a side conversation or a test thread. What if I worked across multiple Codex threads? Submit the Session ID from the thread where the majority of your core functionality was built. If you had multiple significant threads, pick the most representative one. Your README should document how Codex contributed across your workflow. How do I get Codex credits to build? Registered participants can request $100 in free Codex credits to use for this hackathon. Complete the request form at https://forms.gle/Ncu6iGkaHq1SwUmEA before it closes on Friday, July 17th at 12:00 PM PT. Request early — the form will not reopen and Codex credits will not be distributed after that date. The last batch of Codex credits will be delivered shortly after the form closes. One code per Entrant. What if I use up all my Codex credits before the deadline? As stated in the Official Rules: "Any additional charges incurred by the Entrant for the use of OpenAI products or services beyond the provided Codex credits or credits are the responsibility of the Entrant. Entrants are encouraged to monitor their usage so as not to incur additional charges." Watch your usage meter and plan accordingly. How do I check how many Codex credits I have left? Log into chatgpt.com with the account you used to request credits, go to Settings → Usage, and you'll see your credit balance and recent usage. Will I get charged if I run out of credits? No — Codex credits are prepaid. Once they're used up, Codex usage just stops. You won't be charged automatically unless you've turned on Auto top-up in Settings → Usage, so leave that off if you want to be sure you never go over. I want to build with the OpenAI API — can I use my Codex credits for that? You can build with any OpenAI tools, models, or APIs, but per the official rules, your project must be built with Codex and/or GPT‑5.6 to be eligible — quoting the rules directly: "Build any project with Codex and GPT 5.6 that fits into one of the following tracks" and, for projects that existed before the hackathon, they "must have been meaningfully extended using Codex and/or GPT-5.6 after the Submission Period start date." We are only distributing Codex credits for this event — we are not providing separate OpenAI API credits or tokens. Good luck building! Submissions What do I need to submit? A working project built with Codex and GPT-5.6 Your chosen track A text description explaining what you built and how it works A public YouTube demo video (see video requirements above) Provide a URL to your code repository for judging and testing. The repository must be either public (with relevant licensing) or private and shared with testing@devpost.com and build-week-event@openai.com . Include a README with setup instructions, sample data (if needed), and clear guidance for running your project Make sure to highlight where Codex accelerated your workflow, where key decisions were made and how GPT-5.6 and Codex were used . This is an important part of how judges evaluate technical implementation and quality of the idea. Your /feedback Codex Session ID from your primary build thread If you're submitting a Plugin or Developer Tool, also include: installation instructions, supported platforms, and a way for judges to test it without rebuilding from scratch (demo instance, sandbox, or test account). What should be in my README? At minimum: setup instructions, any sample data needed to run the project, and clear guidance on how to test it. Also document how Codex accelerated your workflow, where you made key decisions, and how GPT-5.6 is integrated. This directly feeds into how judges evaluate Technical Implementation and Quality of the Idea. Can judges build my project from scratch to test it? They are not required to. Make it easy — provide a working demo link, test account, or sandbox wherever possible. The easier you make it for judges to see your project working, the better. My project covers multiple tracks. Which do I pick? Pick the one that best fits. If you're genuinely torn, think about the primary audience and use case for your project. You can only enter one track, so choose the closest match. I have a question the FAQ didn't answer. Where do I go? Join the #build-week-chat in the OpenAI Discord or post on the Discussion Board. Demo Video What are the video requirements? Your demo video must: Be 3 minutes or under (judges are not required to watch beyond 3 minutes) Be uploaded to YouTube as a public video Include a clear demo of your working project Include a voiceover (you can use AI to help record or narrate) Cover what you built AND how you used Codex AND how you used GPT-5.6 Wait — does my video really need a voiceover? Yes. This is a stricter requirement than some hackathons. A screencast with background music won't cut it. Judges need to hear, in your own words (or AI-assisted narration), what you built and how you built it. Think of it as a short product demo where you're both the developer and the narrator. What do I need to say about Codex and GPT-5.6? Your voiceover should explain: What your project does How you used Codex to build it (not just that you used it — show the workflow, the key moments, the decisions it helped you make) How GPT-5.6 is integrated into the project and what it's doing You don't have to show the Codex interface on screen, but your narration needs to be specific. "We used Codex to generate the backend" is less compelling than "We used Codex to scaffold the data pipeline and iterate on the API integration — here's what that looked like." Can I use AI to help with my voiceover? Yes. If recording your own voice isn't practical or you just don’t want to, you can use a text-to-speech or AI voice tool to narrate your video.
